date: The Tabuk Expedition, year 9 of the Hijra (630)
title: 24dk3j
The Hadith of the Manzila: at Tabuk, "You are to me as Harun was to Musa"
hook: At Tabuk the Prophet said to Imam Ali, "You are to me as Harun was to Musa."
scenes.0.text: In the ninth year of his migration, the Prophet prepared a great expedition to Tebek in the north. The summer heat was scorching, the road was long, and supplies were scarce. That's why they call it the Army of Trouble. While preparations were underway in Medina, the Prophet called **Ali** to him and asked him to stay in the city this time. This was a surprising decision for those who knew that Ali had been at the Prophet's side in all his battles.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.1.text: Before the army set out, the Prophet entrusted Medina and his family to **Ali**. Women, children, and old men remained in the city. The one who would protect the city and his family while the prophet was away was supposed to be the one he trusted most. Muhammad Ali did not follow the army and remained in Medina, following the order. Staying behind was a sign of trust. The Prophet left his most precious trust to the one he trusted most.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.2.text: As the army moved away from Medina, whispers began in the city. Some began to say that the Prophet did not consider **Ali** worthy of the journey, leaving him behind like a burden. These words reached the ears of Ali, and a thread covered him. He knew these rumors were not true, but he wanted to hear the reason from the Prophet himself. He rode off in the heat of the desert, following the footsteps of the army.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.3.text: **Ali** caught up with the army a short distance from Medina and reached the Prophet. There was a voice in my voice saying, "O Messenger of Allah, are you leaving me with the women and children?" The Prophet did not scold him. He looked at him lovingly and said: "You are to me as Aaron was to Moses. But there is no prophet after me. Don't you agree?" That's the same with Buhari and Muslim. The shadow on Ali's face disappeared. The Prophet did not push it aside, he put it beside him, in the place of Haroun beside **Musa**.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.4.text: When **Ali** received this promise, he turned his horse and returned to Medina. His face and clothes were still covered in dust from the road, but he felt it inside. When he entered the city, the rumors were still going around. But those words no longer mattered to Ali. The Prophet himself had compared his place to that of the brother of Musa, Haroun. Watching over the families in Medina, keeping the city safe and protecting the Prophet's house, now had a whole new meaning in the eyes of Ali. As the army advanced towards Tebek, Ali continued his duty as the Prophet's deputy in Medina.
scenes.5.text: The origin of this metaphor is in the Qur'an. In verses 29-32 of Surah Taha, Moses asks Allah for a helper from his family, saying, "Give me a helper from my family, my brother Aaron. Strengthen me with him, and make him a partner in my affair. And in verse 142 of Surah A'raf, when Moses was going to Mount Tur, he said to Aaron, "Take my place among my people". This is called the Range Hadith, spoken on the way to Tebek. It means range, location and position. The Prophet chose these two examples from the Qur'an to describe Ali's place beside him. Harun (Aaron) was the brother of Musa (Moses), his assistant and deputy in his absence.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.text: Prophecy is clearly distinguished in the range of Hadith, because there will be no other prophet after the Prophet. But the remaining links are too big. Aaron was the brother, assistant and deputy of Moses. The Prophet tied **Ali** to himself with these ties. According to Shia reading, this is a clear sign that Ali will be the leader of the Ummah after the Prophet. Because Aaron was the leader of the people while Moses was away. A few months later, at Ghadir Hum, the Prophet would announce this closeness in front of thousands of pilgrims by raising Ali's hand.
scenes.7.text: Years later, Mu'awiya asked Sahab Sa'd b. Abu Vakkās why he did not curse Ali. In those days, in the minbars of the Embassy, they asked for the curse of Ali. Sa'd counted three recollections he heard from the Prophet. The first was the likeness of Aaron on the road to Tabuk. The second was that the flag was given to Ali in Khyber. The third was that the Prophet took Ali and his family with him on the day of Mubahala. The curse that Mu'awiya wanted was unanswered in the face of the Prophet's words to Ali.

The Prophet
sunni.0.says: The hadith "You are to me as Harun was to Musa."
sunni.1.says: As the Prophet sets out for Tabuk he leaves Imam Ali as deputy in Medina; the Manzila saying.
sunni.2.says: The Manzila hadith with the qualification "there is no prophet after me" (Tabuk); the Mu'awiya-Sa'd conversation.
sunni.3.says: Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas reminds Mu'awiya of three sayings: mawla, Manzila, the Khaybar banner.
shia.0.says: The chains of the Manzila hadith in Shia and Sunni sources and an explanation of its being evidence for the imamate.
disputes.0.title: 1tuz5s
Was the Tabuk arrangement a deputyship or a succession?
disputes.0.sunni: At Tabuk the Prophet left Imam Ali in his place in Medina and spoke the Harun comparison. In the Sunni reading the deputyship is temporary for the length of the expedition; deputies were left on other expeditions too, since Harun died before Musa the saying is not counted as evidence of the caliphate, yet it is still a great virtue.
disputes.0.shia: At Tabuk the Prophet left Imam Ali in his place in Medina and spoke the Harun comparison. In the Shia view Harun is Musa's brother, vizier and caliph; the qualification "except prophethood" shows that the remaining stations were given to Imam Ali.
disputes.1.title: kz4vpp
Is the saying specific to Tabuk, or general?
disputes.1.sunni: The Prophet said this saying at Tabuk so that Imam Ali would not be grieved. In the Sunni reading the saying is limited to that event.
disputes.1.shia: The Prophet said this saying at Tabuk so that Imam Ali would not be grieved. In the Shia view "manzila" is a general position; confining the saying to a single event does not fit its wording.
questions.0: The Prophet separated the prophethood by saying, "There is no prophet after me". Why do you think the Prophet explicitly separated the prophethood and left the rest of the links to Ali?
questions.1: When Ali didn't go to Tebek and stayed in Medina, there were rumors. Why do you think the Prophet chose the example of Moses and Aaron in response to these rumors?
questions.2: There was no sword drawn at Tebek. Why do you think the most memorable event of the expedition was not a battle, but that sentence said to Ali?
summary: In Tabuk, the Prophet said to Ali, "You are to me as Aaron was to Moses". And he said, "There is no prophet after me". This word also occurs in Sunni sources (Buhari, Sahih, no. 3706; Muslim, Sahih, no. 2404). The Shi'a consider this proof that Ali was the Prophet's brother, vizier and caliph.
key: «You are to me as Harun was to Musa»
notes.0: The Tabuk expedition was made in the 9th year of the Hijra against the Byzantine threat.
notes.1: The Prophet left Imam Ali as deputy in Medina.
notes.2: He said, «You are to me as Harun was to Musa; except that there is no prophet after me» (Bukhari 3706, Muslim 2404).
notes.3: This saying describes Imam Ali's place after the Prophet.

scenes.8.text: There was no sword drawn at Tebek. The Prophet returned to Medina with his army after making agreements with the tribes in the region. The trust he left in the city was kept under the care of **Ali**. The most memorable event of the journey was not a battle, but the phrase the Prophet said to his brother, whom he left behind in Medina. This saying has been passed down from generation to generation and has become one of the most remembered hadiths to indicate the location of Ali.
